searchText: > The spec says B should reject, but they could be lenient and request blocks from A, knowing that < 5000 is okay. It is much safer to be backwards-lenient (because you know when to stop request) than forward-lenient (you need to deduce from blocks). > (By backwards lenient, I mean a client that sends you a head after your fork epoch but with the previous fork version... you know you are safe up to the fork epoch) That makes sense to me being backward lenient, we can keep peers around till certain fork epochs/blocks and then disconnect with them when the time is right what's the reason whistleblower rewards for slashable offences aren't included in Phase 0? Whistleblowers are part of phase 1 (it would be trivial for a proposer to rewrite slashing data with their own ID as whistleblower anyway) Why is the whistle blower reward in phase 0? No guarantee the actual whistle blower gets the reward like jim mentioned

excerpts.author: nishant0
excerpts.content:
> The spec says B should reject, but they could be lenient and request blocks from A, knowing that < 5000 is okay. It is much safer to be backwards-lenient (because you know when to stop request) than forward-lenient (you need to deduce from blocks).
> (By backwards lenient, I mean a client that sends you a head after your fork epoch but with the previous fork version... you know you are safe up to the fork epoch)

That makes sense to me being backward lenient, we can keep peers around till certain fork epochs/blocks and then disconnect with them when the time is right
